punchline: Kepler tried to explain planetary motion not with astronomy but with candlelight and a magnet.
thirty_sec: Kepler could not explain why the planets turn. He searched for the answer in comparisons from outside his field: candlelight filling a room, a magnet pulling from a distance. According to David Epstein, Kepler did not cling to one analogy; he compared many, and in the end he saw that orbits are elliptical. On hard questions, an analogy from a distant field often opens a new window.
